title: IPv4: addresses, networks, gateway
summary: What the four numbers of an address mean, what /24 says, and where a packet goes when it leaves your network.

text: An IPv4 address is 32 bits, written as 4 numbers. The /24 after it (the prefix) says how many bits name the network; the rest numbers the machines in it.
- Like a street and a house number: 192.168.1 is the street, 20 the house.
- Machines with the same network part talk to each other directly.
Each bit less in the prefix doubles the network. A /22 is four /24 side by side.
- The first address names the network, the last one is broadcast: a /24 has 254 for machines.
- The private ranges are reused in millions of homes and offices; the internet doesn't route them.
ip -br addr prints one line per network interface.
- lo is the loopback: the machine talking to itself.
- Your real interface is wlan0 (Wi-Fi), eth0 or enp3s0 (cable)… Names vary by machine.
For an address outside its network, the machine hands the packet to the gateway (your router), which passes it on.
- The default route names that gateway. No default route: no internet.
- ip route get asks which route an address would take, without sending anything.
